target.title: feat(customers): configure and extend calendar event types

scenario.action: Open the calendar and launch the new-event editor.
scenario.expected: All configured built-in and module-provided event types are selectable.
scenario.observed: Meeting, Call, Email, Note, Event, Visit, and Task were present and selectable.

scenario.action: Select Visit in the event editor.
scenario.expected: Visit-specific labels and the availability extension render.
scenario.observed: The To recipient field and live 'Selected staff and resources are available' result rendered.

scenario.action: Link a customer, save the Visit, and return to the calendar.
scenario.expected: The create request succeeds and the Visit appears on the calendar.
scenario.observed: The create endpoint returned success, the editor closed, and the saved Visit appeared in the calendar.

scenario.action: Open Calendar settings and follow Manage activity types.
scenario.expected: The control links to the organization-scoped activity-type catalog.
scenario.observed: The link resolved to /backend/config/customers#customer-dictionary-activity-types and loaded the catalog.

scenario.action: Inspect the activity-type catalog and open New activity type.
scenario.expected: Built-in and module types are listed and the grouped configuration form opens.
scenario.observed: All seven types, including example-provided Visit, appeared; Appearance, Form behavior, and Custom-field fieldsets groups loaded.

scenario.action: Open the Visit editor at a 390x844 viewport.
scenario.expected: The full-screen mobile editor remains usable with fixed actions.
scenario.observed: Type controls, scheduling fields, Visit fields, Cancel, and Save event remained reachable without a runtime error.

notes: No console errors, page errors, or genuine failed requests occurred during the completed run.
The real PostgreSQL/HTTP TC-EXAMPLE-018 suite passed all 9 scenarios, including concurrent staff and resource Visit booking races.
Expected Next.js prefetch cancellations reported as net::ERR_ABORTED during navigation were excluded from failed-request results.
The PR includes browser-level integration coverage under customers and the example Visit module, so no follow-up test scenario is required.
